title: feat(pon): measure zero-paired and winner-only W1 strategies
body:
## Why this change

The cheapest legal work baseline must include composition of algorithm choices, actual preparation reuse, and omission of losing proofs. V5 supported lazy generic FullLimb strategies but used the eager legacy entrypoint for its specialized zero integer-paired strategy, leaving that legal combination unmeasured.

This draft is stacked on **#908**. **Whole-chain qualification remains HOLD; production_activation=false.** The experiment's negative result is retained: the same preregistered `full-limb-sparse-lazy` implementation has the lowest aggregate CPU and wall cost per accepted winner in all four cost cells among the five measured strategies.

## Changes and resulting behavior

- Add target-aware `attempt` and cancellable `attempt_with_progress` to the exact-zero producer. Preserve legacy `prove`, reject unsupported operands and the existing invalid zero target, and return an unverified `Attempt` pending full verification and current admission.
- Compare FullLimb sparse eager/lazy, zero-paired legacy, and zero-paired new eager/lazy on matching challenge streams. All arms compute the complete transcript; lazy mode constructs the full proof only after a target hit.
- Charge actual preparation, every miss, losing-proof disposal, winner cleanup and prepared-object teardown. Observe eager proof slices before the producer interval ends, then separately hash all 49,188 actual proof bytes. Audit and verifier intervals are separate and remain in the same process.
- Add strict capture/summary readers and mandatory reader controls. Validate exact types, sequence, identity, roster, first-hit stopping, materialization policy, both full verifiers and correlated-horizon prefixes. Invalid or incomplete evidence yields no comparative rates.
- Retain source-bound evidence, original failures, numerical derivation, all five arms, strategy coverage obligations and incremental corpus pins.

No production default, consensus relation, task authority, target rule, chain weight, reward or receiver budget changes.

## Source identities

| Role | Commit | Scope |

| Native measurements | `165d286b687e0a73d7fe68148d2179274fc0c0b8` | Six completed component shards; full source verification: 28,330 entries / 2,578,833,390 bytes. |
| Final evidence child | `229b14c2d366a257f51f287d502a550df2332338` | Direct docs/evidence/corpus child, tree `b386c32458589f81944ddd69c04a56c28c55e284`; fresh checks below. |
| Parent #908 | `6ac9a79c2fb37d6102c526c354fe2d448a9f4e6d` | C5 remains FAIL 62/64; this component work does not repair those failures. |

The evidence child does not inherit or relabel the native timing source. Its 18 changed paths contain only documents, evidence and the named corpus update; implementation, checker, Cargo and toolchain bytes remain those of the native source.

## Native observation: the lower operation count was not the lowest measured cost

Values are milliseconds per accepted winner: sum of complete producer costs divided by sum of accepted winners within each fixed arm/target/horizon.

| Cell | FullLimb lazy CPU | Zero-paired lazy CPU | FullLimb lazy wall | Zero-paired lazy wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| T0 / H1 | 1.973125 | 2.143376 | 1.978518 | 2.148661 |
| T0 / H8 | 2.414077 | 2.646782 | 2.419570 | 2.651590 |
| T1 / H1 | 51.437078 | 56.326995 | 51.512632 | 56.397523 |
| T1 / H8 | 40.004135 | 44.701399 | 40.065571 | 44.762684 |

T0 is `7f` followed by 31 `ff` bytes; T1 is `07` followed by 31 `ff` bytes. H1/H8 are actual searches per preparation. Each arm/cell has eight cohorts. Separate exhaustion and first-hit controls are excluded from cost comparison.

All six shards reconcile to **240 preparations, 800 searches, 12,840 attempts, 760 hits, 12,080 misses, 40 exhausted searches, 8,008 materialized proofs and 3,280 full-verifier calls**. Matched arms repeat the same streams; these are not 12,840 independent lottery observations. Winners pass both production and scalar-reference full verifiers; their last-product-word mutants are rejected as `Product`. Exhaustion replays retain original miss identity and grant no original-target credit.

Zero-paired lazy versus zero legacy/eager differs by about +/-1%, with mixed direction. Eight-cohort ranges are descriptive, not confidence intervals or stable-advantage claims. Correlated H1/H8 prefixes have different actual attempts per search (T0: 1.5/1.875; T1: 40.5/32.5), so cross-horizon cost changes cannot be attributed only to setup amortization. No per-sample fastest-arm selection or cross-cell pooling is used. Zero-winner cost stays null. Same-process audit/verifier work can affect caches and allocation despite separate clocks; inclusive clocks are not added to components. The numeric excerpt lacks sample IDs and does not independently authenticate pairing or execution.

## Evidence and security limits

See the [evidence README](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/Trillionnium-Chain/blob/229b14c2d366a257f51f287d502a550df2332338/evidence/pon-w1-zero-paired-lazy-20261112/README.md), [complete five-arm tables](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/Trillionnium-Chain/blob/229b14c2d366a257f51f287d502a550df2332338/evidence/pon-w1-zero-paired-lazy-20261112/cost-results.md), [results](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/Trillionnium-Chain/blob/229b14c2d366a257f51f287d502a550df2332338/evidence/pon-w1-zero-paired-lazy-20261112/results.json), [experiment contract](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/Trillionnium-Chain/blob/229b14c2d366a257f51f287d502a550df2332338/docs/research/PON_W1_ZERO_PAIRED_LAZY_V1.md) and [ordered archive parts](https://github.com/TrillionniumFoundation/Trillionnium-Chain/blob/229b14c2d366a257f51f287d502a550df2332338/evidence/pon-w1-zero-paired-lazy-20261112/native-evidence.parts.json).

- Native campaign manifest: 403,864 bytes, SHA256 `1972cd517095034d809b48f509b53dd0d51d24f1b5d37a71bdd0e7c91a5373f6`.
- Retained native ELF SHA256: `106475d07ddd75e0eced90b19ec84a7658732951a207bebd764c37f10a1aace1`.
- Complete byte-verified native archive: **4,591,284 bytes / 784 members**, SHA256 `1f3f04c393e43c1c36fbb8b1569f810d9b8c9b31013d5389410ff2787a252a83`. Ordered raw parts preserve the original reader cap and reassemble every original byte. Archive integrity does not make a failed check pass.

This campaign measures exact zero material on one CPU host, actual nonce/H1/H8 reuse and winner-only proof construction. The README maps all requested strategy classes without claiming completion: nonzero sparse/low-rank/diagonal and real short-column tasks; reuse across miners/epochs; GPU/ASIC, shared caches and early screening; cheap fake-transcript search and receiver rejection; attacker-selected tasks, sponsor self-traffic and repeated rewards; and maintenance without real demand remain separately scoped obligations. Historical observations keep their own source labels.

Generic 262,144 preparation plus 327,680 products per challenge versus 458,752 original-loop products are operation counts. The zero-paired 152,832 count includes 33-bit-sum products. None is a measured speedup or adversarial cost lower bound. Under independent uniform inclusive 256-bit tickets, `p=(T+1)/2^256` and stationary preparation/miss/success costs give `E[C]=P+(1-p)*c_fail/p+c_success`; this finite grid proves neither those assumptions nor a production-parameter security bound. ESA 2026's optimal-adversarial-hardness conjecture does not establish this concrete 64-by-64 relation.

`cheapest_strategy_proven=false`; `production_activation=false`; `consensus_credit=0`. Independent numerical analysis retains `source_execution_authenticated=false`. The lowest observed fixed arm among five is an achievable-cost observation, not a global minimum.

## Publication recovery ledger

The first publication attempt failed during ordinary `git push` with exit 1 and no timeout: the partial clone lacked promisor object `cc716d413f612246f8c4ae90c22facc3578cb93d`. PR creation was not attempted. Source guards before/after agreed. The original receipt remains unchanged: 37,021 bytes, SHA256 `f0dbe2edc4aea351ad49a97f4913d1a2ddd9914a67f776969ef5461d99f58b20`, at `/home/qian-qi/work/w1-baseline-9082-pr-publication/pr-publication-result.json`.

A separate explicit request recovered that 81,462-byte blob, verified the raw Git object SHA1 and raw SHA256 `5067e8a5aef537605a5812391b7a0ae1f0f0670250b7311b2fe62d3e35095b85`, and left repository configuration, index, refs, HEAD, tree and complete source identities unchanged. Before/after remote reads confirmed the branch was absent and no PR existed. Implicit lazy fetching remained disabled. The exact-OID request may bring additional referenced objects; recovery of this object does not claim complete historical closure.

Hydration receipt: 12033 bytes, SHA256 `ead0f3b106e558c71f0caaacddc1ec8b621ec6a1ccb31feb46d746e145faa767`, retained at `/home/qian-qi/work/w1-baseline-9082-explicit-object-hydration/hydration-result.json`.

The second publication attempt uses new create-only helper, body and receipt paths. Its helper changes only the two external OUT/BODY destination constants; reversing those substitutions reproduces the frozen original helper SHA256. All source, account, parent, duplicate-PR, ordinary non-force-push and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` gates remain. The earlier failed attempt is not relabeled successful.

## Second publication refusal and current-child restoration

Attempt 2 was refused by the unchanged complete source guard before any push or PR creation: 115 historical entries again had skip-worktree flags and their physical files were absent. Its before/after guards both failed. Original receipt: 8,658 bytes, SHA256 b00279909cccae3da877d0205b597f4d5278b06087ebb7db7c1db9beb3783bdc, retained at /home/qian-qi/work/w1-baseline-9082-pr-publication-2/pr-publication-result.json. The source of this later state change remains unknown; the shared Git common directory or an index timestamp does not identify a writer.

A new restoration was bound to the exact current child 229b14c2d366a257f51f287d502a550df2332338 and tree b386c32458589f81944ddd69c04a56c28c55e284. It restored 115 missing paths / 800519979 bytes from existing local HEAD blobs, verified raw blob identities and modes, cleared only the observed hidden roster and passed the original complete source guard. It preserved configuration, refused conflicting existing bytes, kept the original double-copy capacity check and requested no fetch. Its source identity exactly equals the independently validated final-child identity above.

Current-child restoration receipt: 308284 bytes, SHA256 eaccd1ccd9f490358e843d5a73dbe1724f6dbf56d5056a2cc4e9359c154e3fe0, retained at /home/qian-qi/work/w1-baseline-9082-index-restoration-229b-1/restoration-result.json. The original restoration, both publication failures and all readback payloads remain separate and unchanged.

Attempt 3 starts immediately after that successful restoration in a separate Python process, preserving the restoration process network restrictions and the publisher process original environment separately. The publisher again uses new OUT/BODY paths with every source, identity, account, parent, duplicate and non-force-push gate unchanged. This is an operational recovery, not a new native campaign or new security qualification.

## Third push failure and bounded pack diagnostics

Attempt 3 passed its source guards but ordinary push returned exit 1, without timeout, for another unavailable historical promisor object: 228a10686f43271638395ab3351a57695564cb1c. No PR creation was attempted. Its original 37,023-byte receipt remains at /home/qian-qi/work/w1-baseline-9082-pr-publication-3/pr-publication-result.json, SHA256 515d076216c1bdf5437647fe5a5c564babf19605149b3870e249eb4a447f9cd0.

An independent no-network object diagnostic fully read all 82 objects in the fixed child-minus-confirmed-parent range (9247019 raw payload bytes), parsed their exact types and sizes, and recomputed every Git object identity. All succeeded. Bounded thin-pack construction also succeeded. Explicit-object and bounded-range full packs with delta search/reuse disabled both produced the same 6,073,233-byte output, SHA256 e0430dd6cb79f1ef02ee3517fb7d9cc9d2d0731a7cf70d501cd53062eef8327b. These are pack-encoding observations; the 82-object pack still references object-graph content already present at the parent, and the bounded range is not claimed identical to a live send-pack input over all advertised remote refs.

Pack diagnostic receipt: 3987 bytes, SHA256 fe25cb881af3ea8896750f86beeae13fc6c421c630de8989f27cef1f6375027f, at /home/qian-qi/work/w1-baseline-9082-pack-closure-diagnostics/summary.json. The new failing historical object was not fetched by an automatic loop.

Attempt 4 changes only external OUT/BODY paths and the transport invocation to git -c pack.window=0 -c push.useBitmaps=false push --no-thin origin HEAD:refs/heads/fix/chain-w1-baseline-20261111-9082. This uses ordinary non-force ref-update semantics and retains the same 600-second push cap, account/origin/parent checks, source guards, duplicate-PR checks and GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1. The two -c settings apply to that command; repository configuration is not rewritten. No --no-verify, forced refspec, missing-object allowance or filter that omits required objects is introduced.

The Git 2.43 [push documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push/2.43.0), [pack documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-pack-objects/2.43.0), and version-pinned [send-pack](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.43.0/send-pack.c) / [pack-objects](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.43.0/builtin/pack-objects.c) code support the narrower encoding choice. The actual publication result remains a separate receipt; the earlier failures are unchanged.
